parts.text:
The subject slides into the booth opposite me, bringing with them the sharp scent of ozone and fear. Up close, the contrast is even more jarring. Beneath the drab, rain-soaked synth-tweed coat, their hands are trembling. They don't belong in the Rainbow District, and right now, they know it better than anyone. 

"You're late," I say, my voice a low rumble that barely cuts beneath the heavy, vibrating bass of *The Prism*. 

They flinch, glancing at the glowing digits on their own wrist-comp. "It's... it's barely past midnight. I had to be sure I wasn't followed."

"At midnight, the perimeter was clear," I reply, my eyes never leaving their face. "At three minutes past, variables change. You're the whistleblower. I'm Erebus. Let's get to the objective. What do you have for me?"

The subject swallows hard, their eyes darting toward the sea of dancers bathed in sweeping laser lights. Slowly, they pull their hand from their coat pocket. They place a small, heavy object on the illuminated tabletop and slide it toward me. It’s a military-grade, bio-encrypted data-slug. Matte black. Unassuming. Worth its weight in blood.

"The intel," they whisper, leaning in close. "Everything is in there. The corporate zoning board isn't just buying out the local leases. They’re planning a localized blackout. A forced purge of the Rainbow District. They want to cut the grid, send in private security under the guise of 'riot control,' and clear out the LGBTQ+ community entirely to build high-yield commercial sectors. The data proves it. The bribes, the blackout codes, the strike teams... it's all there."

I slide the data-slug off the table, palming it seamlessly into my mesh shirt. The cold metal rests against my ribs. *Objective complete.* 

But in this line of work, the data is only half the job. The other half is surviving the extraction. 

My retinal implant pulses with a proximity warning. I shift my gaze past the whistleblower's shoulder, toward the front entrance. The chrome-plated bouncer with the rainbow dreads is currently being shoved aside by three figures pushing their way into the club. They aren't wearing neon. They're wearing tailored, dark suits that bulge unnaturally at the shoulders and ribs—subdermal armor and concealed ballistics. Corporate cleaners. 

"They found me," the whistleblower gasps, following my gaze. Panic spikes in their voice, loud enough to turn the heads of a nearby group of holographic drag performers. 

"Keep your voice down and your head lower," I snap, slipping out of the booth. "The payment has already been routed to your shadow account. Now, we move."

"Where?" 

"Out." 

I grab the back of their tweed coat, pulling them into the densest part of the crowd. We use the chaotic, hyper-saturated brilliance of the dance floor as our camouflage. The cleaners are scanning the booths, their optic implants glowing a faint, menacing red through the heavy vape smoke, but they are looking for a solitary, terrified target—not two people moving in rhythm with the crush of the crowd. 

I guide the subject toward the blind spot I mapped out twenty minutes ago. We slip behind a towering, pulsing speaker column, bypass the automated bar-bots, and hit the heavy steel of the service exit. I slice the mag-lock with a quick burst from my wrist-comp, and we spill out into the cold, rain-slicked alley. 

The heavy thud of the club's bass is instantly muffled as the door seals behind us. The lone saxophone player at the end of the alley is still blowing that mournful, smoky tune, completely oblivious to the corporate hit squad just on the other side of the wall. 

"Go," I tell the whistleblower, pointing down the fire escape route that leads toward the undercity transit lines. "Don't look back, and don't spend the credits all in one place."

They don't hesitate. They vanish into the neon-lit shadows, leaving me alone in the rain. 

I tap the side of my earpiece, the static crackling to life. "Erebus here. Intel gathered. The Rainbow District is about to go to war, and we just got the high ground. Going dark."
